name: Trend across a basket of large coins

sections.hypothesis: Trend-vol-target's rule, applied to each of the 10 most-traded coins in equal slots, earns a better risk-adjusted return than the same coins held equally and than BTC held alone, because diversifying one trend rule across many markets is where trend following's Sharpe comes from.
sections.rationale: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012) found time-series momentum across 58 futures markets, with most of the portfolio's Sharpe from diversification across them. Crypto evidence is mixed: Liu and Tsyvinski (NBER w24877) report significant time-series momentum; a re-examination of Grobys et al. (30 large coins, 2016-23) says the effect is indistinguishable from zero over the full sample. In Kestrel, trend-vol-target passed walk-forward on BTC but failed it on ETH, so it is open whether trend works beyond BTC; this tests that. Differences from the failed cross-sectional momentum: large coins only, slow 20/60/120-day trends, each coin sized to a volatility target, and no ranking by recent winners. Weak points: coins are highly correlated, above all in crashes, so the diversification may vanish exactly when it is needed; large coins by volume include short-lived manias (LUNA, FTT) that later collapsed. Context: after 139+ trials every bet against the trend has failed, cross-sectional momentum over small coins failed (-92% drawdown), and the one strategy marked Pursue is trend-vol-target on BTC daily (Sharpe 1.21 vs 1.07 for holding on the current config, but +639% vs +1,420% return). This note is one of five momentum ideas tested together on 2026-11-13; five ideas at once are five or more trials, so a single pass is weaker evidence than it looks.
sections.rules: Daily bars, whole coin universe (Binance USDT pairs, delisted ones included; stablecoins, fiat, gold and leveraged tokens excluded). Every Sunday's close (UTC): eligible coins have 180+ days of unbroken history and a 30-day median daily volume of 20M USDT or more; the 10 with the highest median volume form the basket. Each gets a slot of 1/10 of equity filled by weight = 1/10 x (average of three votes: close above the close 20, 60 and 120 days earlier) x min(1, 50% / the coin's annualised volatility of its last 30 daily log returns). The rest is cash. Weekly rather than daily, because at a few hundred dollars daily slot changes would mostly be below Binance's minimum order. Decide at the close, trade at the next open; 2% no-trade band; long only, spot; 10 bps fee, square-root impact; spread 1 bp for single-coin runs, by the coin's volume band for universe runs. Every strategy starts cold at the first month: cash until its lookbacks fill, the same convention as every earlier test.
sections.falsification: UNIVERSE 1d, 2020-01 to 2025-10, default parameters, 330 USDT, run once. Comparison: the control large-basket with its defaults (the same 10-coin basket held equally, 180 days of history), run once on the same window and cash. Reject unless all hold: (1) Sharpe above BTC buy-and-hold's (the run's benchmark); (2) Sharpe above the control's; (3) max drawdown no worse than -50%; (4) break-even cost at least twice the cost paid; (5) fewer than 10% of orders rejected (by the exchange minimum), or the result is about account size, not the idea. A pass with a Sharpe below trend-vol-target on BTC (1.21) would show trend generalises but would not replace the BTC strategy; either way it goes to walk-forward first.
sections.parameters: top_n 10, min_history_days 180, min_volume_musd 20, target_vol_pct 50; trend lookbacks 20/60/120 and 30-day volatility fixed as in trend-vol-target. Only these are pre-registered.
sections.costs: Weekly rebalancing of up to 10 coins, each slot changing with its trend votes and volatility; perhaps 15-25x turnover a year. Spreads by volume band: 1-3 bps for the largest coins, up to 15 bps for the smallest in the basket.

history.reason: Pre-registered test (UNIVERSE 1d, 2020-01..2025-10, defaults, 330 USDT; run 20261113-075500-c11ec7, repeated by mistake as 20261113-075724-de8612 with identical results; control large-basket run 20261113-075717-a565e2). Failed rules 1 and 5: Sharpe 0.95 vs 1.07 for BTC buy-and-hold, and 152 of 1,118 orders (13.6%) rejected by the exchange minimum against 10% allowed. Passed 2-4: Sharpe above the control's 0.79, max drawdown -41% (control -85%), break-even 650 bps vs 28 paid. Trend cut the basket's drawdown by half and raised its Sharpe, but the basket of large coins is worse than BTC alone. At 330 USDT ten slots are too small to trade.
